title: I can't see any other nodes
summary: The node list shows only your own radio, or nothing new has appeared for a long time.

steps.question: Is the antenna attached and screwed on firmly?
steps.help: Look at the LoRa antenna, the one the radio shipped with. On boards with a small snap-on lead inside the case, check that the lead is pressed all the way onto its socket.

steps.title: Attach the antenna
steps.body: Without an antenna the radio hears almost nothing, and transmitting without one can damage it.
steps: Turn the radio off or unplug it.
Screw the antenna on finger-tight, or press the snap-on lead onto its socket until it clicks.
Turn the radio back on and give it 15 minutes to hear other nodes.

steps.question: Is the region set to US?
steps.help: In the Meshtastic app, open Settings, then LoRa, and look at Region. A new radio starts with the region unset and does not transmit at all until you choose one.

steps.title: Set the region to US
steps.body: The region decides which frequencies the radio uses. With the wrong one, or none, it is not on the same frequencies as the rest of the Charleston mesh.
steps: Set Region to US and save.
Wait for the radio to restart, then reconnect the app.

links.label: Region settings in the setup guide

steps.question: Is the modem preset LongFast, with the default primary channel?
steps.help: Settings, then LoRa, shows the modem preset: it should read Long Range - Fast (LongFast). Under Channels, the first channel should be the default one, usually listed as LongFast. If you have never changed these, they are already right.

steps.title: Go back to LongFast and the default channel
steps.body: Radios only hear each other when they use the same modem preset and channel. The Charleston mesh uses the Meshtastic defaults.
steps: In Settings, then LoRa, set the modem preset to Long Range - Fast.
Leave the frequency slot at 0, which means the default.
Under Channels, make the first channel the default: no custom name and the default key. Keep any private channels as secondary channels.

steps.question: Has the radio been on, with these settings, for at least 15 minutes?
steps.help: Nodes appear in the list as your radio hears them, and a quiet node may only announce itself every few hours. An empty list in the first minutes is normal.

steps.title: Give it time
steps.body: Your radio has to hear a node before it can list it. Leave it on and let the list fill in.
steps: Leave the radio on for 15 to 30 minutes.
Send a short message on the primary channel. Nearby nodes that repeat it show that you are being heard.

steps.question: Is the radio outdoors or at a window, as high up as you can get it?
steps.help: LoRa needs a mostly clear path between antennas. The Lowcountry is flat, so buildings and trees block the signal quickly. A radio on a desk in the middle of a house often hears nothing.

steps.title: Move the radio higher and into the open
steps.body: Height and a clear view do more for range than any setting.
steps: Put the radio at an upstairs window, on a porch or outside, with the antenna pointing straight up.
Keep it away from metal: window screens, gutters, a car roof.
Look at the network status page to see where nodes are active, and test from somewhere closer to them.

steps.question: Is the radio running a recent stable firmware release?
steps.help: The app shows the firmware version on the screen where you connect to the radio, and tells you when an update is available. A version that is years old may not talk to current radios.

steps.title: Update the firmware
steps.body: Flash the current stable release. Avoid alpha builds unless someone in the community suggested one.
steps: Follow the flashing guide for your board.
Afterwards, check that the region is still US. A full erase resets it.

steps.title: Ask in Discord
steps.body: Your settings look right, so the cause is likely range or something particular to your radio. Someone local can usually tell which.
include: Your region, modem preset and primary channel name
Your neighborhood, and whether the radio is indoors or outdoors and how high up
How long the radio has been on
